title: Least-Recently-Used Cache
statement:
Design a fixed-capacity key-value cache that evicts the entry that has gone unused the longest.

Contract
- `new Solution(capacity)` creates an empty cache holding at most `capacity` entries. Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when `capacity < 1`.
- `get(key)` returns the stored value, or `-1` when the key is absent. Values are non-negative, so `-1` is unambiguous. A successful `get` makes the key the most recently used.
- `put(key, value)` inserts or overwrites. Either way the key becomes the most recently used. When inserting a new key into a full cache, first evict the least recently used key.
- Overwriting an existing key never evicts anything. A `get` that misses changes nothing.
- Both `get` and `put` must run in O(1) average time.

Examples
- With capacity 2: `put(1, 10)`, `put(2, 20)`, `get(1)` returns `10`, `put(3, 30)` evicts key 2, so `get(2)` returns `-1`.
- With capacity 1: `put(1, 5)`, `put(2, 6)` leaves only key 2, so `get(1)` returns `-1` and `get(2)` returns `6`.
- With capacity 2: `put(1, 1)`, `put(2, 2)`, `put(1, 100)`, `put(3, 3)` evicts key 2, and `get(1)` returns `100`.

examples.input: capacity 2: put 1 10, put 2 20, get 1, put 3 30, get 2
capacity 2: put 1 1, put 2 2, put 1 100, put 3 3, get 1, get 2

hints: You need two things at once: find an entry by key quickly, and know which entry was used longest ago. A hash map handles the first, an ordering of entries handles the second.

Keep entries in a doubly linked list ordered by recency, and a map from key to its list node. Moving a node to the front, and removing the node at the back, are both constant time when you can reach the node directly.

Every get hit and every put moves its node to the front; a put into a full cache first removes the tail node and its map entry. Sentinel head and tail nodes remove edge cases. Intended complexity: O(1) time per operation, so n operations take O(n) total (the probe measures a whole run of n operations), and O(capacity) space.
inputSyntax: Input: capacity first, then operations separated by commas, for example: capacity 2, put 1 10, put 2 20, get 1, put 3 30, get 2
